1.0 Introduction
The English language subject is compulsory for all pupils in Standard III-VI.  The significance of teaching and learning English 
language is to promote the mastery of the four language skills (listening, reading, speaking and writing) in Primary Education. 
Therefore, in learning English pupils will build their confidence academically and enable them to communicate with other people 
locally and globally.
The English Language Standard III─VI Syllabus for Primary Education, therefore, is designed to guide teaching and learning 
English for standards III─VI in Mainland Tanzanian. It has been prepared in alignment with the 2023 Basic Education Curriculum. 
This syllabus provides information that will enable teachers to plan their teaching process effectively. In addition, the syllabus 
will enable the teacher to plan teaching and learning activities to develop the pupil’s 21 st century skills of curiosity, creativity, 
collaboration, communication and problem solving.
2.0 Main Objectives of Education in Tanzania
The main objectives of providing education in Tanzania are to enable every Tanzanian to:
(a) Develop and improve his or her personality so that he or she values himself or herself and develops self-confidence;
(b) Respect the culture, traditions and customs of Tanzania; cultural differences; dignity; human rights; attitudes and inclusive 
actions;
(c) Apply science and technology, creativity, critical thinking, innovation, cooperation, communication and positive attitudes 
for his or her development and the sustainable development of the nation and the world at large;
(d) Understand and protect national values, including dignity, patriotism, integrity, unity, transparency, honesty, accountability 
and the national language;
(e) Develop life and work-related skills to increase efficiency in everyday life;
(f) Develop a habit of loving and valuing work to increase productivity and efficiency in production and service provision;
(g) Identify and consider cross-cutting issues, including the health and well-being of the society, gender equality, as well as the 
management and sustainable conservation of the environment; and
(h) Develop national and international cooperation, peace and justice in accordance with the Constitution of the United Republic 
of Tanzania and international conventions.

(h) Recognise and use science and technology in learning and daily life;
(i) Develop knowledge, skills and attitude towards taking care of the environment and respect gender equality, as well as other

6.2  The pupil
The pupil is expected to:
(a)  Develop the intended competences by participating in various learning activities inside and outside the classroom;
(b)  Actively engage in the teaching and learning process; and
(c)  Participate in the search for knowledge from various sources, including textbooks, reference books and other publications 
in online libraries.
6.3 The parent 
The parent/guardian is expected to do the following:
(a) Monitor the child’s academic progress in school;
(b) Where possible, provide the child with the needed academic support;
(c) Provide the child with a safe and friendly home environment that is conducive for learning;
(d) Keep track of the child progress in behaviour;
(e) Provide the child with any materials required in the learning process; and
(f) Instil in the child a sense of commitment and positive value towards education. 
7.0 Teaching and Learning Methods
The teaching and learning methods are instrumental in developing pupil’s intended competences. This syllabus suggests teaching 
and learning methods for each activity. They are aimed at enabling pupils to interact with content, which includes listening to and/
or watching live or recorded materials, engaging with a written or visual text, and engaging with multimedia. All these aim to help 
pupils develop listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills as well as develop vocabulary and grammar. However, a teacher is 
advised to use other appropriate methods based on the environment or context.

6
8.0 Teaching and Learning Resources
The process of teaching and learning requires different resources. In that regard, both a teacher and pupil should work together to 
collect or improvise alternative resources available in the school and home environment when needed. The teacher and pupil are 
expected to constantly seek for information from various sources to effectively facilitate teaching and learning process. The list of 
approved textbooks and references books shall be provided by the TIE.
9.0 Assessment 
Assessment is an important process in the learning and teaching process to facilitate the development of intended competences. 
The assessment of the English language will involve continuous and summative assessment. The continuous assessment will 
take into account the criteria in each learning activity and will enable the teacher to determine the pupil’s learning ability and 
needs. It will also help the teacher to assess pupils knowledge, skills and attitudes and the ability to use the four language skills in 
various contexts. Furthermore, the assessment information will enable the teacher to improve teaching and learning to facilitate the 
pupil’s achievement of the intended outcomes. The assessment tools that will be used during teaching and learning are, checklists, 
classroom exercises, home works, questionnaires, face-to-face questions, practical works (individual and group works), project 
works and portfolios and other similar tools.  
The final assessment will include weekly, monthly, terminal and annual examinations which will be used to assess pupil’s learning 
progress and provide feedback to facilitate teaching and learning process. In addition, there will be a standard six national assessment 
that will contribute 7.5% marks to the Form Four National Examination.

7
10.0   Number of Periods
The English Language Syllabus for Primary Education Standard III─VI provides estimates of the time that will be spent in teaching 
and learning, in consideration of the complexity of the specific competences and the learning activities.  Therefore, seven periods 
of 40 minutes each have been allocated for this subject per week for Standard III and IV and six periods of 40 minutes each have 
been allocated for this subject per week for Standard V and VI respectively.

The contents of this subject are presented in matrix form with seven columns which include main competences, specific 
competences, learning activities, suggested teaching and learning methods, assessment criteria, resources and the number of 
periods as presented in Tables 2–5.

Standard III.table_name: Table 2: Detailed Contents for Standard III

main_competences.main_title: Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

specific_competences.title: Develop listening and speaking skills

learning_activities.activity: Write dictated words
learning_activities.methods: Dictation: Guide the pupils through writing words (use only words that the pupil has already learned to spell)
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Dictated words are written correctly
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials for listening and speaking

learning_activities.activity: Listen and respond to questions based on simple stories from familiar contexts (home, school)
learning_activities.methods: Prediction: Show the pupils a cover of a book to predict what the story is about. Storytelling: Tell the pupils a story using facial expressions, voices and gestures to support understanding.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Questions on simple stories in a familiar environment are responded to correctly
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials for listening and speaking

specific_competences.title: Develop phonemic awareness and pronunciation of English letters

learning_activities.activity: Read aloud simple short stories
learning_activities.methods: Discussion: Give the pupils a list of words and guide them through pronouncing familiar words. Songs: Guide the pupils through singing songs with targeted words.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple and short texts are read aloud fluently
learning_activities.resources: Manila paper, cards, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with phonemes

learning_activities.activity: Read short, simple texts for comprehension
learning_activities.methods: Demonstration: Demonstrate by reading a text and asking comprehension questions. Scanning: Guide the pupils through picking and combining specific words from a text to generate the general idea.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Short texts are read for comprehension
learning_activities.resources: Manila paper, cards, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with phonemes

specific_competences.title: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing

learning_activities.activity: Use personal pronouns
learning_activities.methods: Matching: Use pictures to guide the pupils through pronouncing the words him, her, it, them, you, etc. Songs: Guide the pupils through singing songs with pronouns and ask them some questions about the pronouns.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Personal pronouns are used correctly
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express possession using the verbs have and has
learning_activities.methods: Describing: Guide the pupils through expressing possessions using have and has. Draw and Describe: Ask the pupils to draw pictures and describe them using have and has.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Possessions are well expressed using the verbs have and has
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express routines and ongoing activities in school and home contexts (target: simple present tense, present continuous tense)
learning_activities.methods: Demonstration: Demonstrate the use and structure of simple present tense, and present continuous tense. Chart: Use a chart with columns for the simple present and present continuous process to show the pupils how -s, -es and -ies are added to the verb. Pictures: Show the pupils a series of pictures with sentences underneath narrating what is happening in the images.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Routines and ongoing activities in school and home contexts are expressed correctly
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: and, but)
learning_activities.methods: Songs: Play recorded songs about conjunctions and ask the pupils to identify the conjunctions. Explanation: Compose pairs of simple sentences for pupils to see how and and but are used.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are used in oral and written contexts
learning_activities.resources: Texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

specific_competences.title: Read a variety of simple texts appropriately

learning_activities.activity: Read two-syllable and grade-appropriate words
learning_activities.methods: Explain and demonstrate: Demonstrate and explain the structure of syllables. Syllable Match-Ups: Give the pupils cards with single syllables to match up and make new two-syllable words.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Two syllables and grade-appropriate words are read correctly
learning_activities.resources: Various reading texts

learning_activities.activity: Read multi-syllable and grade-appropriate words
learning_activities.methods: Clapping Games: Guide the pupils through identifying syllables in spoken words by clapping for each syllable. Jumping syllables: Lead the pupils to separate words into syllables and create new words. Songs: Use fun songs such as The Wheels on the Bus, Old McDonald, The Itsy Bitsy Spider, Bingo, and Row Row Row Your Boat to learn to pronounce words into syllables. Using pictures: Guide the pupils through identifying and saying multi syllabic words from magazines or online sources.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Multi-syllable and grade-appropriate words are read correctly
learning_activities.resources: Various reading texts

learning_activities.activity: Read aloud a variety of grade-level texts
learning_activities.methods: Modelling: Read a text aloud then ask the pupils to read the texts after you have read. Question and Answer: Ask questions before, during and after reading a text.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: A variety of grade-level texts are read aloud
learning_activities.resources: Various reading texts

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Identify words with short and long vowels (e.g., ship/sheep, full/fool, to/too)
learning_activities.methods: Read and write: Guide the pupils through pronouncing and writing words with long vowels. Sort the words: Guide pupils through sorting the words based on how long vowel sounds are spelled.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words with short and long vowels are identified
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Pronounce words with long vowel sounds with speed and fluency
learning_activities.methods: Discussion: Ask the pupils to discuss and circle the correct spelling of words with long vowel sounds.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words with long vowels are pronounced with speed and fluency
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Read short phrases and simple sentences with short and long vowels
learning_activities.methods: Instructional routines: Guide the pupils through using 'touch and say' to read phrases containing long vowels.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Short phrases and simple sentences with short and long vowels are read correctly
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

main_competences.main_title: Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

specific_competences.title: Develop vocabulary by relating words with objects in the environment

learning_activities.activity: Associate words with objects found in different contexts (e.g., home, hospital, market, bus station)
learning_activities.methods: Direct/explicit instruction: Guide the pupils through learning words in their immediate surroundings. Repetition and multiple exposures: Expose the pupils to new words.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words are associated with objects found in different contexts
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts and audio/audiovisual materials with environmental vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Match objects with their respective characteristics
learning_activities.methods: Vocabulary 7-up game: Guide the pupils through matching vocabulary with objects in a simple game.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words are matched with their respective characteristics
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts and audio/audiovisual materials with environmental vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Construct short sentences using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.methods: Word walls: Ask the pupils to construct sentences with words on the word wall.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Short sentences are constructed by using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts and audio/audiovisual materials with environmental vocabulary

specific_competences.title: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing

learning_activities.activity: Talk about quantity using appropriate words (e.g., some, many, any, much)
learning_activities.methods: Explanation: Guide the pupils through talking about quantities of things using some, many, any, much. Role play: Guide the pupils through playing the roles of sellers and buyers in shopping using the expressions 'How much is it' and 'How many do we want/need'.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Quantities are expressed using appropriate words
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express location using appropriate prepositions of place and time (target: in, at, on, under, inside, outside, over, near)
learning_activities.methods: Games: Use games like 'Simon Says' to guide the pupils through responding to commands with prepositions. Preposition race: Ask the pupils to follow instructions that include prepositions of place and time.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Location is expressed using appropriate prepositions of place and time
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express past events (target: simple past tense, past continuous tense)
learning_activities.methods: Game: Ask the pupils to change irregular verbs in present tense into past tense.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Past events are expressed correctly
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: so, because)
learning_activities.methods: Link-Up Game: Guide the pupils in pairs through writing a sentence at the same time using so and because. 'SLAP-IT' Game: Guide the pupils through getting the correct word and gaining a point for their group in the game.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are well used in oral and written contexts
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

specific_competences.title: Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context

learning_activities.activity: Participate in simple dialogues about school, market and home contexts
learning_activities.methods: Dialogue: Use a dialogue with the appropriate vocabulary for market and home. Roleplay: Guide the pupils through role-playing a teacher-pupil conversation on a particular topic.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple dialogues are produced on school, market and home contexts
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with communicative contexts

specific_competences.title: Read appropriately a variety of simple texts

learning_activities.activity: Read aloud grade-level simple texts with appropriate intonation
learning_activities.methods: Demonstration: Read aloud, model, and verbalize the words in the text. Reader's Theatre: Assign the pupils in groups to take turns in reading their scripts with appropriate intonation.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level simple texts are read aloud with appropriate intonation
learning_activities.resources: Simple texts with a variety of topics

learning_activities.activity: Read grade-level simple texts of different natures fluently
learning_activities.methods: Modelling: Reading simple texts and ask the pupils to read in groups.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level simple texts of different natures are read fluently
learning_activities.resources: Simple texts with a variety of topics

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Pronounce words with similar sounds (e.g., see/sea, by/bye/buy, right/write)
learning_activities.methods: Listen and Repeat: Pronounce a word and ask your pupils to pronounce it after you. Tongue twisters: Guide the pupils through reciting tongue twisters with the correct pronunciation.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words with the same sound are pronounced correctly
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Convey simple ideas using words with similar sounds
learning_activities.methods: Modelling: Construct complete and correct sentences with two words with the same sound. Discussion: Guide the pupils through discussing a particular topic.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple ideas are conveyed using words with the same sound
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Use words with opposite meanings in spoken contexts
learning_activities.methods: Brainstorming: Lead the pupils in groups to compose sentences using the antonyms of given words. Matching: Guide the pupils through matching words with their antonyms. Complete the list: Assign the pupils to complete the column of antonyms for each word provided in another column. Memory games: Mix words and their antonyms and ask the pupils to match them.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Words with opposite meanings are used in spoken contexts
learning_activities.resources: Wallcharts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with features of spoken language

specific_competences.title: Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Identify the form and content of wishes and messages
learning_activities.methods: Task-based learning: Guide the pupils through identifying the form and content of written messages from a sample of cards.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The form and content of wishes and messages are identified
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts, calendars, cards and audio/audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Write wishes and messages to parents, teachers and friends
learning_activities.methods: Guided writing: Guide the pupils through writing their wishes in groups. Games: Guide the pupils through using the 'Association game' to write messages to parents, teachers and friends.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Wishes and messages are written to parents, teachers and friends correctly
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts, calendars, cards and audio/audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Prepare a schedule of daily routines
learning_activities.methods: Match up: Guide the pupils through matching different times of the day with their daily routine. Composing: Guide the pupils through composing their schedules for daily routines.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Schedules of daily routines are prepared correctly
learning_activities.resources: Realia, word lists, charts, calendars, cards and audio/audiovisual materials with appropriate vocabulary

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing

learning_activities.activity: Write simple sentences using visual/audiovisual stimuli (e.g., pictures, charts, diagrams)
learning_activities.methods: Pictures: Use pictures to guide the pupils through describing and writing sentences. Mix and fix sentences: Guide the pupils through constructing sentences by re-arranging mixed parts of sentences. What's missing? Guide the pupils through identifying the skipped parts or sentences.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple sentences are written using visual/audiovisual stimuli
learning_activities.resources: Picture, charts, diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

learning_activities.activity: Write simple guided paragraphs using appropriate conjunctions and punctuation marks (target: and, but, comma, full stop, question marks)
learning_activities.methods: Brainstorming: Ask the pupils to brainstorm on a chosen topic. Hook-On Sentences: Guide the pupils to write simple guided paragraphs by hooking one sentence to another.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple guided paragraphs are written using appropriate conjunctions and punctuation marks
learning_activities.resources: Picture, charts, diagrams and simple texts with a variety of issues

learning_activities.activity: Construct short passages using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings

'Do As I Say' Game: Guide the pupils through using commands with prepositions to move into different positions. The List Challenger: Guide the pupils through creating sentences using the given prepositions.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Location is expressed using appropriate prepositions of direction
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express possession using adjectives and pronouns (target: my, mine, yours, his, her, hers, their, theirs)

learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Possessions are expressed using adjectives and pronouns
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Express completed and unfinished actions (structure: present perfect, past perfect tense)
learning_activities.methods: Dialogue: Prepare a dialogue using present perfect and past perfect tenses and let the pupils practice it. I know What You Will Say Game: Lead the pupils in groups to complete questions using the present perfect or past simple.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Completed and unfinished actions are expressed correctly
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: too... to, either... or, neither... nor)
learning_activities.methods: Songs: Play recorded songs with conjunctions for pupils to identify and sing. Read and choose: Guide the pupils through reading sentences and choosing correct conjunctions. Sentence completion: Guide the pupils through completing sentences with missing conjunctions.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Conjunctions are used in oral and written contexts
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Use active and passive voices in oral and written contexts
learning_activities.methods: Matching: Provide active and passive voice sentences on cards for pupils to match. Rewriting: Guide the pupils through rewriting sentences from active to passive voice.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Active and passive voices are used in oral and written contexts
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with grammar and vocabulary

specific_competences.title: Comprehend information presented orally

learning_activities.activity: Follow oral instructions from different contexts (e.g., instructions on taking medicines, recipe, drawing, making things)
learning_activities.methods: Role-play: Guide the pupils through role-playing scenarios with oral instructions (e.g., a doctor and a patient).
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Oral instructions from different contexts are followed
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with oral instructions

learning_activities.activity: Listen to and record messages from different sources
learning_activities.methods: Dictation: Dictate messages for the pupils to record. Group listening: Have the pupils listen to an audio message and take notes.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Messages from different sources are listened to and recorded
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with oral instructions

learning_activities.activity: Identify major ideas from conversations in familiar contexts
learning_activities.methods: Listening and summarizing: Have pupils listen to dialogues and extract key themes.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Major ideas from conversations in familiar contexts are identified
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with oral instructions

learning_activities.activity: Summarise main ideas of a story presented orally
learning_activities.methods: Oral retelling: Ask pupils to retell the story outline in 3-4 sentences.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Main ideas of a story presented orally are summarised
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with oral instructions

learning_activities.activity: Retell oral stories in logical sequence
learning_activities.methods: Timeline storytelling: Have pupils use sequential connectors (first, then, next, finally) to recount a story.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Oral stories are retold in logical sequence
learning_activities.resources: Charts, texts and audio/audiovisual materials with oral instructions

specific_competences.title: Construct meaning from simple texts

learning_activities.activity: Read grade-level texts on cross-cutting issues (e.g. corruption, gender, child rights, environment)
learning_activities.methods: Guided reading: Guide pupils through reading thematic texts and discussing core issues.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level texts on cross-cutting issues are read and understood
learning_activities.resources: Texts, leaflets, posters on cross-cutting themes

learning_activities.activity: Deduce meaning of unfamiliar words using contextual clues
learning_activities.methods: Context detective: Ask pupils to identify surrounding keywords that clarify unknown words.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Meaning of unfamiliar words is deduced using contextual clues
learning_activities.resources: Texts, leaflets, posters on cross-cutting themes

learning_activities.activity: Summarise information presented in a text
learning_activities.methods: Paragraph reduction: Guide pupils to reduce a 3-paragraph text to main bullet points.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Information presented in a text is accurately summarised
learning_activities.resources: Texts, leaflets, posters on cross-cutting themes

specific_competences.title: Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context

learning_activities.activity: Identify main ideas from conversations on familiar communicative contexts (e.g. at the post office, police station, bank)
learning_activities.methods: Simulated field scenarios: Create mock post office and banking dialogues.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Main ideas from conversations in familiar contexts are identified
learning_activities.resources: Realia, mock banking slips, stamps, dialogue audio

learning_activities.activity: Respond to questions based on conversations in familiar communicative contexts
learning_activities.methods: Role-play Q&A: Pairs ask and answer realistic institutional questions.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Questions based on institutional conversations are responded to accurately
learning_activities.resources: Realia, mock banking slips, stamps, dialogue audio

specific_competences.title: Read appropriately a variety of simple texts

learning_activities.activity: Read aloud grade-level texts with appropriate pronunciation and intonation
learning_activities.methods: Pronunciation drills and choral reading: Pupils practice rhythm and sentence stress.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Grade-level texts are read aloud with correct stress, intonation and pronunciation
learning_activities.resources: Graded readers, literary anthologies, audio recordings

learning_activities.activity: Reading silently for comprehension and pleasure
learning_activities.methods: Silent sustained reading (SSR): Allocate 15 minutes of independent quiet reading followed by a log entry.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Pupils demonstrate comprehension from silent reading through targeted checks
learning_activities.resources: Graded readers, literary anthologies, audio recordings

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Practise falling and rising intonation in questions and statements
learning_activities.methods: Pitch graphing: Draw pitch arrows on the board to illustrate rising question pitch and falling statements.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Falling and rising intonation patterns are demonstrated correctly
learning_activities.resources: Audio clips, flashcards with punctuation pitch cues

learning_activities.activity: Practise word stress in compound and multi-syllable words
learning_activities.methods: Stress tapping: Tap desk loudly on accented syllable (e.g. DOC-tor, po-TATO).
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Word stress is placed correctly on accented syllables
learning_activities.resources: Audio clips, flashcards with punctuation pitch cues

learning_activities.activity: Use question tags in conversational contexts (e.g. isn't it?, aren't you?, didn't they?)
learning_activities.methods: Tag completion games: Pupils complete partner prompts with matching auxiliary tag.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Question tags are used correctly in oral communication
learning_activities.resources: Audio clips, flashcards with punctuation pitch cues

specific_competences.title: Produce short and basic oral messages with a logical structure and intelligible pronunciation

learning_activities.activity: Make statements about objects and ideas that can be judged as true or false
learning_activities.methods: Fact check game: Pupils give factual statements about geography and science for peers to evaluate.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Statements that can be verified as true or false are clearly formulated
learning_activities.resources: Fact cards, picture scenes, science charts

learning_activities.activity: Present simple speeches about self and family members on familiar topics (e.g. my pet, my brother, birthday party, wedding)
learning_activities.methods: Show and tell: Pupils bring an object or photo and deliver a 2-minute structured oral presentation.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Simple speeches on familiar topics are delivered with logical flow and clear pronunciation
learning_activities.resources: Family photos, personal artifacts, cue cards

specific_competences.title: Produce short written messages using appropriate grammar and vocabulary

learning_activities.activity: Identify the form and content of appreciation, thanks and apology notes
learning_activities.methods: Text structural analysis: Examine realia samples of polite notes and identify salutation, reason, and closing.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Structural elements of notes of appreciation, gratitude and apology are identified
learning_activities.resources: Sample greeting cards, letter templates, envelopes

learning_activities.activity: Write appreciation, thanks and apology notes to teachers, friends and parents
learning_activities.methods: Guided letter drafting: Pupils draft personal thank-you notes for real school events.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Polite notes are drafted with appropriate tone, correct spelling and standard layout
learning_activities.resources: Sample greeting cards, letter templates, envelopes

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate basic skills in creative writing

learning_activities.activity: Create a journal to record inspiring things (at home, at school, from TV and radio programmes, etc.)
learning_activities.methods: Personal diary keeping: Maintain a weekly reflective diary with prompt starters.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Personal journals are created and maintained with reflective entries
learning_activities.resources: Journal notebooks, prompt cards, literary magazines

learning_activities.activity: Devise a topic for a poem from the ideas recorded in a journal
learning_activities.methods: Mind mapping: Extract central emotional themes from journal entries into poetic titles.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Poetic themes and titles are generated from journal material
learning_activities.resources: Journal notebooks, prompt cards, literary magazines

learning_activities.activity: Use basic figures of speech (simile, metaphor, personification) to write a four-line stanza
learning_activities.methods: Poetic devices workshop: Create comparative phrases using 'as... as' and 'like', building into a 4-line rhymed or unrhymed stanza.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: A 4-line stanza incorporating similes, metaphors or personification is composed
learning_activities.resources: Anthologies of children's poetry, figurative language charts

main_competences.main_title: Demonstrate mastery of basic English language skills

specific_competences.title: Develop vocabulary by relating words with objects in the environment

learning_activities.activity: Compose a dialogue using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.methods: Brainstorming and scriptwriting: Guide pupils through writing and dramatising realistic dialogues set in agricultural, airport, and trade environments.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Dialogue is composed using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.resources: Realia, environmental word lists, role-play props

learning_activities.activity: Compose a story using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.methods: Guided narrative composition: Pupils compose a cohesive short story integrating specialized contextual nouns.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: A story is composed using vocabulary referring to objects found in different settings
learning_activities.resources: Realia, environmental word lists, role-play props

specific_competences.title: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary both orally and in writing

learning_activities.activity: Express nationalities using appropriate adjectives (e.g. Tanzanian, Japanese, Norwegian)
learning_activities.methods: Country-to-nationality matching: World maps and flags used to practice proper adjective suffixes (-ian, -ese, -ish).
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Nationalities are expressed accurately using proper descriptive adjectives
learning_activities.resources: World maps, national flags, identity cards, travel documents

learning_activities.activity: Use relative pronouns in appropriate contexts (e.g., who, whose, whom)
learning_activities.methods: Sentence combining: Merge two simple clauses into a complex sentence using relative pronouns.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Relative pronouns who, whose, and whom are used accurately in defining clauses
learning_activities.resources: Sentence strips, grammar substitution tables

learning_activities.activity: Express future actions (structure: will, shall, going to)
learning_activities.methods: Future planning: Pupils write and talk about career aspirations and planned holiday schedules.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Future intentions and predictions are expressed using will, shall, and going to
learning_activities.resources: Calendars, career charts, weather forecasts

learning_activities.activity: Use conjunctions in oral and written contexts (target: yet, despite, in spite of, so... that)
learning_activities.methods: Contrastive conjunction drills: Construct complex sentences expressing concession and cause-effect.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Concessive and result conjunctions are used correctly in speech and writing
learning_activities.resources: Charts with conjunction matrices, reading texts

learning_activities.activity: Express conditional situations (target: Conditional Type 1 & Type 2: if + present -> will; if + past -> would)
learning_activities.methods: Hypothetical question chains: 'If you won a prize, what would you do?' oral practice.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Conditional clauses type 1 and 2 are constructed with accurate verb forms
learning_activities.resources: Conditional prompt cards, game boards

specific_competences.title: Comprehend information presented orally

learning_activities.activity: Report orally information from radio, TV and online broadcasts
learning_activities.methods: Broadcast summary: Pupils listen to a simulated news broadcast and deliver an oral headline brief.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Key information from broadcast media is accurately reported orally
learning_activities.resources: Radio recordings, news transcripts, audio playback devices

learning_activities.activity: Participate in conversations on contemporary social issues (e.g. climate change, digital safety, health)
learning_activities.methods: Fishbowl discussions: Small groups discuss current national and global issues.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Pupils engage actively in discussions using substantiated points
learning_activities.resources: Articles, posters on national environmental and health issues

learning_activities.activity: Engage in oral presentations based on research or project findings
learning_activities.methods: Mini-project defense: Present findings from a simple survey or school inquiry.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Oral presentations are delivered clearly with supporting arguments
learning_activities.resources: Project charts, survey question sheets

specific_competences.title: Construct meaning from simple texts

learning_activities.activity: Interpret figurative and idiomatic language from a text (e.g. idioms, riddles, proverbs)
learning_activities.methods: Idiom decoding: Match common English idioms and proverbs with their figurative meanings.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Figurative and idiomatic expressions are correctly interpreted in context
learning_activities.resources: Dictionary of idioms, proverb collection cards

learning_activities.activity: Infer meaning from a text
learning_activities.methods: Reading between the lines: Deduce author attitude, unstated motives, and implied outcomes.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Implied meanings and inferences are correctly drawn from written texts
learning_activities.resources: Short mystery stories, allegorical passages

learning_activities.activity: Relate the content of a text with real life
learning_activities.methods: Text-to-self / text-to-world connections: Discuss how characters' dilemmas apply to local communities.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Textual themes are thoughtfully connected to real-life situations
learning_activities.resources: Narrative passages reflecting community life

specific_competences.title: Respond appropriately in a familiar communicative context

learning_activities.activity: Give an appropriate and logical conclusion to a conversation
learning_activities.methods: Dialogue resolution: Provide truncated dialogue scripts for pupils to compose an effective conclusion.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Logical, polite, and communicative conclusions are provided for conversations
learning_activities.resources: Role-play transcripts, community interaction cards

learning_activities.activity: Debate on topical issues (e.g. gender, entrepreneurship, corruption, education)
learning_activities.methods: Structured parliamentary debate: Proposition and opposition teams debate motions with timed speeches.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Arguments on topical motions are articulated persuasively and respectfully
learning_activities.resources: Debate guidelines, scorecards, topic briefs

learning_activities.activity: Give appropriate responses to riddles
learning_activities.methods: Riddle contest: Solve and compose creative riddles requiring wordplay and logic.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Riddles are decoded and solved using analytical language skills
learning_activities.resources: Traditional and modern English riddle anthologies

specific_competences.title: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic features of spoken language

learning_activities.activity: Express feelings using appropriate intonation patterns (e.g., surprise, shock, happiness, sadness)
learning_activities.methods: Emotion intonation drills: Speak identical sentences with varying pitch contours to reflect diverse emotional states.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Vocal pitch, stress, and intonation accurately convey intended emotional feelings
learning_activities.resources: Audio recordings, emoji prompt cards, theatre scripts

learning_activities.activity: Use appropriate backchannels in conversations (e.g. so, well, right, uh-huh, wow, yeah, really)
learning_activities.methods: Active listening simulations: Practice realistic conversational listening cues during peer dialogues.
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: Conversational backchannels are deployed naturally to sustain dialogue
learning_activities.resources: Dialogue transcripts, conversational audio clips
